variable {L : Language}
variable {M : Type*} {M₁ : Type*} {M₂ : Type*} {M₃ : Type*}

  [s : Structure L M] [s₁ : Structure L M₁] [s₂ : Structure L M₂] [s₃ : Structure L M₃]

namespace Structure

variable (L M M₁ M₂ M₃)

structure Hom where
  toFun : M₁ → M₂
  func' : ∀ {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → M₁), toFun (s₁.func f v) = s₂.func f (toFun ∘ v)
  rel' : ∀ {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁), s₁.rel r v → s₂.rel r (toFun ∘ v)

notation:25 M " →ₛ[" L "] " M' => Hom L M M'

structure Embedding extends M₁ →ₛ[L] M₂ where
  toFun_inj : Function.Injective toFun
  rel_inv' {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁) : s₂.rel r (toFun ∘ v) → s₁.rel r v

notation:25 M " ↪ₛ[" L "] " M' => Embedding L M M'

structure Iso extends M₁ ↪ₛ[L] M₂ where
  toFun_bij : Function.Bijective toFun

notation:25 M " ≃ₛ[" L "] " M' => Iso L M M'

@[ext] structure ClosedSubset where
  domain : Set M
  domain_closed : ∀ {k} (f : L.Func k) {v : Fin k → M}, (∀ i, v i ∈ domain) → s.func f v ∈ domain

class HomClass (F : Type*) (L : outParam (Language.{u}))
    (M₁ : outParam (Type*)) (M₂ : outParam (Type*)) [s₁ : Structure L M₁] [s₂ : Structure L M₂] [FunLike F M₁ M₂] where
  map_func : ∀ (h : F) {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → M₁), h (func f v) = func f (h ∘ v)
  map_rel : ∀ (h : F) {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁), s₁.rel r v → s₂.rel r (h ∘ v)

class EmbeddingClass (F : Type*) (L : outParam (Language.{u}))
    (M₁ : outParam (Type*)) (M₂ : outParam (Type*)) [s₁ : Structure L M₁] [s₂ : Structure L M₂] [FunLike F M₁ M₂]
    extends HomClass F L M₁ M₂ where
  map_inj (f : F) : Function.Injective f
  map_rel_inv (f : F) {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁) : s₂.rel r (f ∘ v) → s₁.rel r v

class IsoClass (F : Type*) (L : outParam (Language.{u}))
    (M₁ : outParam (Type*)) (M₂ : outParam (Type*)) [s₁ : Structure L M₁] [s₂ : Structure L M₂] [FunLike F M₁ M₂]
    extends EmbeddingClass F L M₁ M₂ where
  map_bij (f : F) : Function.Bijective f

variable {L M M₁ M₂ M₃}

instance : FunLike (M₁ →ₛ[L] M₂) M₁ M₂ where
  coe := fun φ => φ.toFun
  coe_injective' := fun φ ψ h => by rcases φ; rcases ψ; simp at h ⊢; ext; exact congr_fun h _

instance : HomClass (M₁ →ₛ[L] M₂) L M₁ M₂ where
  map_func := Hom.func'
  map_rel := Hom.rel'

omit [Nonempty M₁] [Nonempty M₂]

protected lemma rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁) :
    s₁.rel r v → s₂.rel r (φ ∘ v) := map_rel φ r v

lemma val_term (e : Fin n → M₁) (ε : ξ → M₁) (t : Semiterm L ξ n) :
    φ (t.val s₁ e ε) = t.val s₂ (φ ∘ e) (φ ∘ ε) := by
  induction t <;> simp [*, Semiterm.val_func, HomClass.func, Function.comp_def]

end HomClass

instance : FunLike (M₁ ↪ₛ[L] M₂) M₁ M₂ where
  coe := fun φ => φ.toFun
  coe_injective' := fun φ ψ h => by rcases φ; rcases ψ; simp at h ⊢; ext; exact congr_fun h _

protected lemma rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁) :
    s₂.rel r (φ ∘ v) ↔ s₁.rel r v := ⟨map_rel_inv φ r v, HomClass.rel φ r v⟩

  map_rel_inv := fun φ => φ.rel_inv'

end IsoClass

namespace ClosedSubset

variable (u : ClosedSubset L M)

instance : SetLike (ClosedSubset L M) M := ⟨ClosedSubset.domain, fun _ _ ↦ ClosedSubset.ext⟩

omit [Nonempty M]
lemma closed {k} (f : L.Func k) {v : Fin k → M} (hv : ∀ i, v i ∈ u) : s.func f v ∈ u := u.domain_closed f hv

instance toStructure [s : Structure L M] (u : ClosedSubset L M) : Structure L u where
  func := fun k f v => ⟨s.func f (fun i ↦ ↑(v i)), u.closed f (by simp)⟩
  rel := fun k r v => s.rel r (fun i ↦ v i)

protected lemma func {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → u) : u.toStructure.func f v = s.func f (fun i ↦ v i) := rfl

protected lemma rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → u) : u.toStructure.rel r v ↔ s.rel r (fun i ↦ v i) := of_eq rfl

def inclusion : u ↪ₛ[L] M where
  toFun := Subtype.val
  func' := by simp [ClosedSubset.func, Function.comp_def]
  rel' := by simp [ClosedSubset.rel, Function.comp_def]
  rel_inv' := by simp [ClosedSubset.rel, Function.comp_def]
  toFun_inj := Subtype.val_injective

end ClosedSubset

end Structure

namespace Semiformula
open Structure

variable {F : Type*} [FunLike F M₁ M₂] [EmbeddingClass F L M₁ M₂] (Θ : F)
variable {e₁ : Fin n → M₁} {ε₁ : ξ → M₁}

omit [Nonempty M₁] [Nonempty M₂]
lemma eval_hom_iff_of_open {n} {e₁ : Fin n → M₁} {ε₁ : ξ → M₁} : {φ : Semiformula L ξ n} → φ.Open →
    (Eval s₁ e₁ ε₁ φ ↔ Eval s₂ (Θ ∘ e₁) (Θ ∘ ε₁) φ)
  | ⊤,        _ => by simp
  | ⊥,        _ => by simp
  | rel r v,  _ => by simp [Function.comp_def, eval_rel, ←EmbeddingClass.rel Θ, HomClass.val_term]
  | nrel r v, _ => by simp [Function.comp_def, eval_nrel, ←EmbeddingClass.rel Θ, HomClass.val_term]
  | φ ⋏ ψ,    h => by simp at h ⊢; simp [eval_hom_iff_of_open h.1, eval_hom_iff_of_open h.2]
  | φ ⋎ ψ,    h => by simp at h ⊢; simp [eval_hom_iff_of_open h.1, eval_hom_iff_of_open h.2]

lemma eval_hom_univClosure {n} {ε₁ : ξ → M₁} {φ : Semiformula L ξ n} (hp : φ.Open) :
    Evalf s₂ (Θ ∘ ε₁) (∀* φ) → Evalf s₁ ε₁ (∀* φ) := by
  simp; intro h e₁; exact (eval_hom_iff_of_open Θ hp).mpr (h (Θ ∘ e₁))

end Semiformula

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic.Semantics.Semantics

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

section

variable {L : Language}
variable {M : Type*} {M₁ : Type*} {M₂ : Type*} {M₃ : Type*}
variable [Nonempty M] [Nonempty M₁] [Nonempty M₂] [Nonempty M₃]
  [s : Structure L M] [s₁ : Structure L M₁] [s₂ : Structure L M₂] [s₃ : Structure L M₃]

namespace Structure

variable (L M M₁ M₂ M₃)

structure Hom where
  toFun : M₁ → M₂
  func' : ∀ {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → M₁), toFun (s₁.func f v) = s₂.func f (toFun ∘ v)
  rel' : ∀ {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁), s₁.rel r v → s₂.rel r (toFun ∘ v)

notation:25 M " →ₛ[" L "] " M' => Hom L M M'

structure Embedding extends M₁ →ₛ[L] M₂ where
  toFun_inj : Function.Injective toFun
  rel_inv' {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁) : s₂.rel r (toFun ∘ v) → s₁.rel r v

notation:25 M " ↪ₛ[" L "] " M' => Embedding L M M'

structure Iso extends M₁ ↪ₛ[L] M₂ where
  toFun_bij : Function.Bijective toFun

notation:25 M " ≃ₛ[" L "] " M' => Iso L M M'

@[ext] structure ClosedSubset where
  domain : Set M
  domain_closed : ∀ {k} (f : L.Func k) {v : Fin k → M}, (∀ i, v i ∈ domain) → s.func f v ∈ domain

class HomClass (F : Type*) (L : outParam (Language.{u}))
    (M₁ : outParam (Type*)) (M₂ : outParam (Type*)) [s₁ : Structure L M₁] [s₂ : Structure L M₂] [FunLike F M₁ M₂] where
  map_func : ∀ (h : F) {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → M₁), h (func f v) = func f (h ∘ v)
  map_rel : ∀ (h : F) {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁), s₁.rel r v → s₂.rel r (h ∘ v)

class EmbeddingClass (F : Type*) (L : outParam (Language.{u}))
    (M₁ : outParam (Type*)) (M₂ : outParam (Type*)) [s₁ : Structure L M₁] [s₂ : Structure L M₂] [FunLike F M₁ M₂]
    extends HomClass F L M₁ M₂ where
  map_inj (f : F) : Function.Injective f
  map_rel_inv (f : F) {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁) : s₂.rel r (f ∘ v) → s₁.rel r v

class IsoClass (F : Type*) (L : outParam (Language.{u}))
    (M₁ : outParam (Type*)) (M₂ : outParam (Type*)) [s₁ : Structure L M₁] [s₂ : Structure L M₂] [FunLike F M₁ M₂]
    extends EmbeddingClass F L M₁ M₂ where
  map_bij (f : F) : Function.Bijective f

variable {L M M₁ M₂ M₃}

instance : FunLike (M₁ →ₛ[L] M₂) M₁ M₂ where
  coe := fun φ => φ.toFun
  coe_injective' := fun φ ψ h => by rcases φ; rcases ψ; simp at h ⊢; ext; exact congr_fun h _

instance : HomClass (M₁ →ₛ[L] M₂) L M₁ M₂ where
  map_func := Hom.func'
  map_rel := Hom.rel'

omit [Nonempty M₁] [Nonempty M₂]
@[ext] lemma Hom.ext (φ ψ : M₁ →ₛ[L] M₂) (h : ∀ x, φ x = ψ x) : φ = ψ := DFunLike.ext φ ψ h

namespace HomClass

variable {F : Type*} [FunLike F M₁ M₂] [HomClass F L M₁ M₂] (φ : F)

@[ext] lemma ext (φ ψ : F) (h : ∀ x, φ x = ψ x) : φ = ψ := DFunLike.ext φ ψ h

protected lemma func {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → M₁) :
    φ (s₁.func f v) = s₂.func f (φ ∘ v) := map_func φ f v

protected lemma rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁) :
    s₁.rel r v → s₂.rel r (φ ∘ v) := map_rel φ r v

lemma val_term (e : Fin n → M₁) (ε : ξ → M₁) (t : Semiterm L ξ n) :
    φ (t.val s₁ e ε) = t.val s₂ (φ ∘ e) (φ ∘ ε) := by
  induction t <;> simp [*, Semiterm.val_func, HomClass.func, Function.comp_def]

end HomClass

instance : FunLike (M₁ ↪ₛ[L] M₂) M₁ M₂ where
  coe := fun φ => φ.toFun
  coe_injective' := fun φ ψ h => by rcases φ; rcases ψ; simp at h ⊢; ext; exact congr_fun h _

instance : EmbeddingClass (M₁ ↪ₛ[L] M₂) L M₁ M₂ where
  map_func := fun φ => φ.func'
  map_rel := fun φ => φ.rel'
  map_inj := Embedding.toFun_inj
  map_rel_inv := fun φ => φ.rel_inv'

@[ext] lemma Embedding.ext (φ ψ : M₁ ↪ₛ[L] M₂) (h : ∀ x, φ x = ψ x) : φ = ψ := DFunLike.ext φ ψ h

namespace EmbeddingClass
open HomClass
variable {F : Type*} [FunLike F M₁ M₂] [EmbeddingClass F L M₁ M₂] (φ : F)

def toEmbedding : M₁ ↪ M₂ where
  toFun := φ
  inj'  := map_inj φ

protected lemma func {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → M₁) :
    φ (s₁.func f v) = s₂.func f (φ ∘ v) := map_func φ f v

protected lemma rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁) :
    s₂.rel r (φ ∘ v) ↔ s₁.rel r v := ⟨map_rel_inv φ r v, HomClass.rel φ r v⟩

end EmbeddingClass

instance : FunLike (M₁ ≃ₛ[L] M₂) M₁ M₂ where
  coe := fun φ => φ.toFun
  coe_injective' := fun φ ψ h => by rcases φ; rcases ψ; simp at h ⊢; ext; exact congr_fun h _

instance : IsoClass (M₁ ≃ₛ[L] M₂) L M₁ M₂ where
  map_func := fun φ => φ.func'
  map_rel := fun φ => φ.rel'
  map_inj := fun φ => φ.toFun_inj
  map_rel_inv := fun φ => φ.rel_inv'
  map_bij := fun φ => φ.toFun_bij

@[ext] lemma Iso.ext (φ ψ : M₁ ≃ₛ[L] M₂) (h : ∀ x, φ x = ψ x) : φ = ψ := DFunLike.ext φ ψ h

namespace IsoClass

end IsoClass

namespace ClosedSubset

variable (u : ClosedSubset L M)

instance : SetLike (ClosedSubset L M) M := ⟨ClosedSubset.domain, fun _ _ ↦ ClosedSubset.ext⟩

omit [Nonempty M]
lemma closed {k} (f : L.Func k) {v : Fin k → M} (hv : ∀ i, v i ∈ u) : s.func f v ∈ u := u.domain_closed f hv

instance toStructure [s : Structure L M] (u : ClosedSubset L M) : Structure L u where
  func := fun k f v => ⟨s.func f (fun i ↦ ↑(v i)), u.closed f (by simp)⟩
  rel := fun k r v => s.rel r (fun i ↦ v i)

protected lemma func {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → u) : u.toStructure.func f v = s.func f (fun i ↦ v i) := rfl

protected lemma rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → u) : u.toStructure.rel r v ↔ s.rel r (fun i ↦ v i) := of_eq rfl

def inclusion : u ↪ₛ[L] M where
  toFun := Subtype.val
  func' := by simp [ClosedSubset.func, Function.comp_def]
  rel' := by simp [ClosedSubset.rel, Function.comp_def]
  rel_inv' := by simp [ClosedSubset.rel, Function.comp_def]
  toFun_inj := Subtype.val_injective

end ClosedSubset

end Structure

namespace Semiformula
open Structure

variable {F : Type*} [FunLike F M₁ M₂] [EmbeddingClass F L M₁ M₂] (Θ : F)
variable {e₁ : Fin n → M₁} {ε₁ : ξ → M₁}

omit [Nonempty M₁] [Nonempty M₂]
lemma eval_hom_iff_of_open {n} {e₁ : Fin n → M₁} {ε₁ : ξ → M₁} : {φ : Semiformula L ξ n} → φ.Open →
    (Eval s₁ e₁ ε₁ φ ↔ Eval s₂ (Θ ∘ e₁) (Θ ∘ ε₁) φ)
  | ⊤,        _ => by simp
  | ⊥,        _ => by simp
  | rel r v,  _ => by simp [Function.comp_def, eval_rel, ←EmbeddingClass.rel Θ, HomClass.val_term]
  | nrel r v, _ => by simp [Function.comp_def, eval_nrel, ←EmbeddingClass.rel Θ, HomClass.val_term]
  | φ ⋏ ψ,    h => by simp at h ⊢; simp [eval_hom_iff_of_open h.1, eval_hom_iff_of_open h.2]
  | φ ⋎ ψ,    h => by simp at h ⊢; simp [eval_hom_iff_of_open h.1, eval_hom_iff_of_open h.2]

lemma eval_hom_univClosure {n} {ε₁ : ξ → M₁} {φ : Semiformula L ξ n} (hp : φ.Open) :
    Evalf s₂ (Θ ∘ ε₁) (∀* φ) → Evalf s₁ ε₁ (∀* φ) := by
  simp; intro h e₁; exact (eval_hom_iff_of_open Θ hp).mpr (h (Θ ∘ e₁))

end Semiformula

end

lemma refl (M) [Nonempty M] [Structure L M] : M ≡ₑ[L] M := fun σ => by rfl

@[symm]
lemma symm : (M₁ ≡ₑ[L] M₂) → (M₂ ≡ₑ[L] M₁) :=
  fun h σ => (h σ).symm

@[trans]
lemma trans :
    (M₁ ≡ₑ[L] M₂) → (M₂ ≡ₑ[L] M₃) → (M₁ ≡ₑ[L] M₃) :=
  fun h₁ h₂ σ => Iff.trans (h₁ σ) (h₂ σ)

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic.Semantics.Semantics

namespace LO

variable {L : Language}
variable {M : Type*} {M₁ : Type*} {M₂ : Type*} {M₃ : Type*}
variable [Nonempty M] [Nonempty M₁] [Nonempty M₂] [Nonempty M₃]
  [s : Structure L M] [s₁ : Structure L M₁] [s₂ : Structure L M₂] [s₃ : Structure L M₃]

namespace Structure

variable (L M M₁ M₂ M₃)

structure Hom where
  toFun : M₁ → M₂
  func' : ∀ {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → M₁), toFun (s₁.func f v) = s₂.func f (toFun ∘ v)
  rel' : ∀ {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁), s₁.rel r v → s₂.rel r (toFun ∘ v)

notation:25 M " →ₛ[" L "] " M' => Hom L M M'

structure Embedding extends M₁ →ₛ[L] M₂ where
  toFun_inj : Function.Injective toFun
  rel_inv' {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁) : s₂.rel r (toFun ∘ v) → s₁.rel r v

notation:25 M " ↪ₛ[" L "] " M' => Embedding L M M'

structure Iso extends M₁ ↪ₛ[L] M₂ where
  toFun_bij : Function.Bijective toFun

notation:25 M " ≃ₛ[" L "] " M' => Iso L M M'

@[ext] structure ClosedSubset where
  domain : Set M
  domain_closed : ∀ {k} (f : L.Func k) {v : Fin k → M}, (∀ i, v i ∈ domain) → s.func f v ∈ domain

class HomClass (F : Type*) (L : outParam (Language.{u}))
    (M₁ : outParam (Type*)) (M₂ : outParam (Type*)) [s₁ : Structure L M₁] [s₂ : Structure L M₂] [FunLike F M₁ M₂] where
  map_func : ∀ (h : F) {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → M₁), h (func f v) = func f (h ∘ v)
  map_rel : ∀ (h : F) {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁), s₁.rel r v → s₂.rel r (h ∘ v)

class EmbeddingClass (F : Type*) (L : outParam (Language.{u}))
    (M₁ : outParam (Type*)) (M₂ : outParam (Type*)) [s₁ : Structure L M₁] [s₂ : Structure L M₂] [FunLike F M₁ M₂]
    extends HomClass F L M₁ M₂ where
  map_inj (f : F) : Function.Injective f
  map_rel_inv (f : F) {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁) : s₂.rel r (f ∘ v) → s₁.rel r v

class IsoClass (F : Type*) (L : outParam (Language.{u}))
    (M₁ : outParam (Type*)) (M₂ : outParam (Type*)) [s₁ : Structure L M₁] [s₂ : Structure L M₂] [FunLike F M₁ M₂]
    extends EmbeddingClass F L M₁ M₂ where
  map_bij (f : F) : Function.Bijective f

variable {L M M₁ M₂ M₃}

instance : FunLike (M₁ →ₛ[L] M₂) M₁ M₂ where
  coe := fun φ => φ.toFun
  coe_injective' := fun φ ψ h => by rcases φ; rcases ψ; simp at h ⊢; ext; exact congr_fun h _

instance : HomClass (M₁ →ₛ[L] M₂) L M₁ M₂ where
  map_func := Hom.func'
  map_rel := Hom.rel'

omit [Nonempty M₁] [Nonempty M₂]
@[ext] lemma Hom.ext (φ ψ : M₁ →ₛ[L] M₂) (h : ∀ x, φ x = ψ x) : φ = ψ := DFunLike.ext φ ψ h

namespace HomClass

variable {F : Type*} [FunLike F M₁ M₂] [HomClass F L M₁ M₂] (φ : F)

@[ext] lemma ext (φ ψ : F) (h : ∀ x, φ x = ψ x) : φ = ψ := DFunLike.ext φ ψ h

protected lemma func {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → M₁) :
    φ (s₁.func f v) = s₂.func f (φ ∘ v) := map_func φ f v

protected lemma rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁) :
    s₁.rel r v → s₂.rel r (φ ∘ v) := map_rel φ r v

lemma val_term (e : Fin n → M₁) (ε : ξ → M₁) (t : Semiterm L ξ n) :
    φ (t.val s₁ e ε) = t.val s₂ (φ ∘ e) (φ ∘ ε) := by
  induction t <;> simp [*, Semiterm.val_func, HomClass.func, Function.comp_def]

end HomClass

instance : FunLike (M₁ ↪ₛ[L] M₂) M₁ M₂ where
  coe := fun φ => φ.toFun
  coe_injective' := fun φ ψ h => by rcases φ; rcases ψ; simp at h ⊢; ext; exact congr_fun h _

instance : EmbeddingClass (M₁ ↪ₛ[L] M₂) L M₁ M₂ where
  map_func := fun φ => φ.func'
  map_rel := fun φ => φ.rel'
  map_inj := Embedding.toFun_inj
  map_rel_inv := fun φ => φ.rel_inv'

@[ext] lemma Embedding.ext (φ ψ : M₁ ↪ₛ[L] M₂) (h : ∀ x, φ x = ψ x) : φ = ψ := DFunLike.ext φ ψ h

namespace EmbeddingClass
open HomClass
variable {F : Type*} [FunLike F M₁ M₂] [EmbeddingClass F L M₁ M₂] (φ : F)

def toEmbedding : M₁ ↪ M₂ where
  toFun := φ
  inj'  := map_inj φ

protected lemma func {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → M₁) :
    φ (s₁.func f v) = s₂.func f (φ ∘ v) := map_func φ f v

protected lemma rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁) :
    s₂.rel r (φ ∘ v) ↔ s₁.rel r v := ⟨map_rel_inv φ r v, HomClass.rel φ r v⟩

end EmbeddingClass

instance : FunLike (M₁ ≃ₛ[L] M₂) M₁ M₂ where
  coe := fun φ => φ.toFun
  coe_injective' := fun φ ψ h => by rcases φ; rcases ψ; simp at h ⊢; ext; exact congr_fun h _

instance : IsoClass (M₁ ≃ₛ[L] M₂) L M₁ M₂ where
  map_func := fun φ => φ.func'
  map_rel := fun φ => φ.rel'
  map_inj := fun φ => φ.toFun_inj
  map_rel_inv := fun φ => φ.rel_inv'
  map_bij := fun φ => φ.toFun_bij

@[ext] lemma Iso.ext (φ ψ : M₁ ≃ₛ[L] M₂) (h : ∀ x, φ x = ψ x) : φ = ψ := DFunLike.ext φ ψ h

namespace IsoClass

end IsoClass

namespace ClosedSubset

variable (u : ClosedSubset L M)

instance : SetLike (ClosedSubset L M) M := ⟨ClosedSubset.domain, fun _ _ ↦ ClosedSubset.ext⟩

omit [Nonempty M]
lemma closed {k} (f : L.Func k) {v : Fin k → M} (hv : ∀ i, v i ∈ u) : s.func f v ∈ u := u.domain_closed f hv

instance toStructure [s : Structure L M] (u : ClosedSubset L M) : Structure L u where
  func := fun k f v => ⟨s.func f (fun i ↦ ↑(v i)), u.closed f (by simp)⟩
  rel := fun k r v => s.rel r (fun i ↦ v i)

protected lemma func {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → u) : u.toStructure.func f v = s.func f (fun i ↦ v i) := rfl

protected lemma rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → u) : u.toStructure.rel r v ↔ s.rel r (fun i ↦ v i) := of_eq rfl

def inclusion : u ↪ₛ[L] M where
  toFun := Subtype.val
  func' := by simp [ClosedSubset.func, Function.comp_def]
  rel' := by simp [ClosedSubset.rel, Function.comp_def]
  rel_inv' := by simp [ClosedSubset.rel, Function.comp_def]
  toFun_inj := Subtype.val_injective

end ClosedSubset

end Structure

namespace Semiformula
open Structure

variable {F : Type*} [FunLike F M₁ M₂] [EmbeddingClass F L M₁ M₂] (Θ : F)
variable {e₁ : Fin n → M₁} {ε₁ : ξ → M₁}

lemma eval_hom_iff_of_open {n} {e₁ : Fin n → M₁} {ε₁ : ξ → M₁} : {φ : Semiformula L ξ n} → φ.Open →
    (Eval s₁ e₁ ε₁ φ ↔ Eval s₂ (Θ ∘ e₁) (Θ ∘ ε₁) φ)
  | ⊤,        _ => by simp
  | ⊥,        _ => by simp
  | rel r v,  _ => by simp [Function.comp_def, eval_rel, ←EmbeddingClass.rel Θ, HomClass.val_term]
  | nrel r v, _ => by simp [Function.comp_def, eval_nrel, ←EmbeddingClass.rel Θ, HomClass.val_term]
  | φ ⋏ ψ,    h => by simp at h ⊢; simp [eval_hom_iff_of_open h.1, eval_hom_iff_of_open h.2]
  | φ ⋎ ψ,    h => by simp at h ⊢; simp [eval_hom_iff_of_open h.1, eval_hom_iff_of_open h.2]

lemma eval_hom_univClosure {n} {ε₁ : ξ → M₁} {φ : Semiformula L ξ n} (hp : φ.Open) :
    Evalf s₂ (Θ ∘ ε₁) (∀* φ) → Evalf s₁ ε₁ (∀* φ) := by
  simp; intro h e₁; exact (eval_hom_iff_of_open Θ hp).mpr (h (Θ ∘ e₁))

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic.Semantics.Semantics

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

section

variable {L : Language}
variable {M : Type*} {M₁ : Type*} {M₂ : Type*} {M₃ : Type*}
variable [Nonempty M] [Nonempty M₁] [Nonempty M₂] [Nonempty M₃]
  [s : Structure L M] [s₁ : Structure L M₁] [s₂ : Structure L M₂] [s₃ : Structure L M₃]

namespace Structure

variable (L M M₁ M₂ M₃)

structure Hom where
  toFun : M₁ → M₂
  func' : ∀ {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → M₁), toFun (s₁.func f v) = s₂.func f (toFun ∘ v)
  rel' : ∀ {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁), s₁.rel r v → s₂.rel r (toFun ∘ v)

notation:25 M " →ₛ[" L "] " M' => Hom L M M'

structure Embedding extends M₁ →ₛ[L] M₂ where
  toFun_inj : Function.Injective toFun
  rel_inv' {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁) : s₂.rel r (toFun ∘ v) → s₁.rel r v

notation:25 M " ↪ₛ[" L "] " M' => Embedding L M M'

structure Iso extends M₁ ↪ₛ[L] M₂ where
  toFun_bij : Function.Bijective toFun

lemma eval_hom_iff_of_open {n} {e₁ : Fin n → M₁} {ε₁ : ξ → M₁} : {φ : Semiformula L ξ n} → φ.Open →
    (Eval s₁ e₁ ε₁ φ ↔ Eval s₂ (Θ ∘ e₁) (Θ ∘ ε₁) φ)
  | ⊤,        _ => by simp
  | ⊥,        _ => by simp
  | rel r v,  _ => by simp [Function.comp_def, eval_rel, ←EmbeddingClass.rel Θ, HomClass.val_term]
  | nrel r v, _ => by simp [Function.comp_def, eval_nrel, ←EmbeddingClass.rel Θ, HomClass.val_term]
  | φ ⋏ ψ,    h => by simp at h ⊢; simp [eval_hom_iff_of_open h.1, eval_hom_iff_of_open h.2]
  | φ ⋎ ψ,    h => by simp at h ⊢; simp [eval_hom_iff_of_open h.1, eval_hom_iff_of_open h.2]

lemma eval_hom_univClosure {n} {ε₁ : ξ → M₁} {φ : Semiformula L ξ n} (hp : φ.Open) :
    Evalf s₂ (Θ ∘ ε₁) (∀* φ) → Evalf s₁ ε₁ (∀* φ) := by
  simp; intro h e₁; exact (eval_hom_iff_of_open Θ hp).mpr (h (Θ ∘ e₁))

end Semiformula

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic.Semantics.Semantics

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

section

variable {L : Language}
variable {M : Type*} {M₁ : Type*} {M₂ : Type*} {M₃ : Type*}
variable [Nonempty M] [Nonempty M₁] [Nonempty M₂] [Nonempty M₃]
  [s : Structure L M] [s₁ : Structure L M₁] [s₂ : Structure L M₂] [s₃ : Structure L M₃]

namespace Structure

variable (L M M₁ M₂ M₃)

structure Hom where
  toFun : M₁ → M₂
  func' : ∀ {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → M₁), toFun (s₁.func f v) = s₂.func f (toFun ∘ v)
  rel' : ∀ {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁), s₁.rel r v → s₂.rel r (toFun ∘ v)

notation:25 M " →ₛ[" L "] " M' => Hom L M M'

structure Embedding extends M₁ →ₛ[L] M₂ where
  toFun_inj : Function.Injective toFun
  rel_inv' {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁) : s₂.rel r (toFun ∘ v) → s₁.rel r v

notation:25 M " ↪ₛ[" L "] " M' => Embedding L M M'

structure Iso extends M₁ ↪ₛ[L] M₂ where
  toFun_bij : Function.Bijective toFun

notation:25 M " ≃ₛ[" L "] " M' => Iso L M M'

@[ext] structure ClosedSubset where
  domain : Set M
  domain_closed : ∀ {k} (f : L.Func k) {v : Fin k → M}, (∀ i, v i ∈ domain) → s.func f v ∈ domain

class HomClass (F : Type*) (L : outParam (Language.{u}))
    (M₁ : outParam (Type*)) (M₂ : outParam (Type*)) [s₁ : Structure L M₁] [s₂ : Structure L M₂] [FunLike F M₁ M₂] where
  map_func : ∀ (h : F) {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → M₁), h (func f v) = func f (h ∘ v)
  map_rel : ∀ (h : F) {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁), s₁.rel r v → s₂.rel r (h ∘ v)

class EmbeddingClass (F : Type*) (L : outParam (Language.{u}))
    (M₁ : outParam (Type*)) (M₂ : outParam (Type*)) [s₁ : Structure L M₁] [s₂ : Structure L M₂] [FunLike F M₁ M₂]
    extends HomClass F L M₁ M₂ where
  map_inj (f : F) : Function.Injective f
  map_rel_inv (f : F) {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁) : s₂.rel r (f ∘ v) → s₁.rel r v

class IsoClass (F : Type*) (L : outParam (Language.{u}))
    (M₁ : outParam (Type*)) (M₂ : outParam (Type*)) [s₁ : Structure L M₁] [s₂ : Structure L M₂] [FunLike F M₁ M₂]
    extends EmbeddingClass F L M₁ M₂ where
  map_bij (f : F) : Function.Bijective f

variable {L M M₁ M₂ M₃}

instance : FunLike (M₁ →ₛ[L] M₂) M₁ M₂ where
  coe := fun φ => φ.toFun
  coe_injective' := fun φ ψ h => by rcases φ; rcases ψ; simp at h ⊢; ext; exact congr_fun h _

instance : HomClass (M₁ →ₛ[L] M₂) L M₁ M₂ where
  map_func := Hom.func'
  map_rel := Hom.rel'

omit [Nonempty M₁] [Nonempty M₂]
@[ext] lemma Hom.ext (φ ψ : M₁ →ₛ[L] M₂) (h : ∀ x, φ x = ψ x) : φ = ψ := DFunLike.ext φ ψ h

namespace HomClass

variable {F : Type*} [FunLike F M₁ M₂] [HomClass F L M₁ M₂] (φ : F)

@[ext] lemma ext (φ ψ : F) (h : ∀ x, φ x = ψ x) : φ = ψ := DFunLike.ext φ ψ h

protected lemma func {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → M₁) :
    φ (s₁.func f v) = s₂.func f (φ ∘ v) := map_func φ f v

protected lemma rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁) :
    s₁.rel r v → s₂.rel r (φ ∘ v) := map_rel φ r v

lemma val_term (e : Fin n → M₁) (ε : ξ → M₁) (t : Semiterm L ξ n) :
    φ (t.val s₁ e ε) = t.val s₂ (φ ∘ e) (φ ∘ ε) := by
  induction t <;> simp [*, Semiterm.val_func, HomClass.func, Function.comp_def]

end HomClass

instance : FunLike (M₁ ↪ₛ[L] M₂) M₁ M₂ where
  coe := fun φ => φ.toFun
  coe_injective' := fun φ ψ h => by rcases φ; rcases ψ; simp at h ⊢; ext; exact congr_fun h _

instance : EmbeddingClass (M₁ ↪ₛ[L] M₂) L M₁ M₂ where
  map_func := fun φ => φ.func'
  map_rel := fun φ => φ.rel'
  map_inj := Embedding.toFun_inj
  map_rel_inv := fun φ => φ.rel_inv'

@[ext] lemma Embedding.ext (φ ψ : M₁ ↪ₛ[L] M₂) (h : ∀ x, φ x = ψ x) : φ = ψ := DFunLike.ext φ ψ h

namespace EmbeddingClass
open HomClass
variable {F : Type*} [FunLike F M₁ M₂] [EmbeddingClass F L M₁ M₂] (φ : F)

def toEmbedding : M₁ ↪ M₂ where
  toFun := φ
  inj'  := map_inj φ

protected lemma func {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → M₁) :
    φ (s₁.func f v) = s₂.func f (φ ∘ v) := map_func φ f v

protected lemma rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁) :
    s₂.rel r (φ ∘ v) ↔ s₁.rel r v := ⟨map_rel_inv φ r v, HomClass.rel φ r v⟩

end EmbeddingClass

instance : FunLike (M₁ ≃ₛ[L] M₂) M₁ M₂ where
  coe := fun φ => φ.toFun
  coe_injective' := fun φ ψ h => by rcases φ; rcases ψ; simp at h ⊢; ext; exact congr_fun h _

instance : IsoClass (M₁ ≃ₛ[L] M₂) L M₁ M₂ where
  map_func := fun φ => φ.func'
  map_rel := fun φ => φ.rel'
  map_inj := fun φ => φ.toFun_inj
  map_rel_inv := fun φ => φ.rel_inv'
  map_bij := fun φ => φ.toFun_bij

@[ext] lemma Iso.ext (φ ψ : M₁ ≃ₛ[L] M₂) (h : ∀ x, φ x = ψ x) : φ = ψ := DFunLike.ext φ ψ h

namespace IsoClass

end IsoClass

namespace ClosedSubset

variable (u : ClosedSubset L M)

instance : SetLike (ClosedSubset L M) M := ⟨ClosedSubset.domain, fun _ _ ↦ ClosedSubset.ext⟩

omit [Nonempty M]
lemma closed {k} (f : L.Func k) {v : Fin k → M} (hv : ∀ i, v i ∈ u) : s.func f v ∈ u := u.domain_closed f hv

instance toStructure [s : Structure L M] (u : ClosedSubset L M) : Structure L u where
  func := fun k f v => ⟨s.func f (fun i ↦ ↑(v i)), u.closed f (by simp)⟩
  rel := fun k r v => s.rel r (fun i ↦ v i)

protected lemma func {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → u) : u.toStructure.func f v = s.func f (fun i ↦ v i) := rfl

protected lemma rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → u) : u.toStructure.rel r v ↔ s.rel r (fun i ↦ v i) := of_eq rfl

def inclusion : u ↪ₛ[L] M where
  toFun := Subtype.val
  func' := by simp [ClosedSubset.func, Function.comp_def]
  rel' := by simp [ClosedSubset.rel, Function.comp_def]
  rel_inv' := by simp [ClosedSubset.rel, Function.comp_def]
  toFun_inj := Subtype.val_injective

end ClosedSubset

end Structure

namespace Semiformula
open Structure

variable {F : Type*} [FunLike F M₁ M₂] [EmbeddingClass F L M₁ M₂] (Θ : F)
variable {e₁ : Fin n → M₁} {ε₁ : ξ → M₁}

omit [Nonempty M₁] [Nonempty M₂]
lemma eval_hom_iff_of_open {n} {e₁ : Fin n → M₁} {ε₁ : ξ → M₁} : {φ : Semiformula L ξ n} → φ.Open →
    (Eval s₁ e₁ ε₁ φ ↔ Eval s₂ (Θ ∘ e₁) (Θ ∘ ε₁) φ)
  | ⊤,        _ => by simp
  | ⊥,        _ => by simp
  | rel r v,  _ => by simp [Function.comp_def, eval_rel, ←EmbeddingClass.rel Θ, HomClass.val_term]
  | nrel r v, _ => by simp [Function.comp_def, eval_nrel, ←EmbeddingClass.rel Θ, HomClass.val_term]
  | φ ⋏ ψ,    h => by simp at h ⊢; simp [eval_hom_iff_of_open h.1, eval_hom_iff_of_open h.2]
  | φ ⋎ ψ,    h => by simp at h ⊢; simp [eval_hom_iff_of_open h.1, eval_hom_iff_of_open h.2]

lemma eval_hom_univClosure {n} {ε₁ : ξ → M₁} {φ : Semiformula L ξ n} (hp : φ.Open) :
    Evalf s₂ (Θ ∘ ε₁) (∀* φ) → Evalf s₁ ε₁ (∀* φ) := by
  simp; intro h e₁; exact (eval_hom_iff_of_open Θ hp).mpr (h (Θ ∘ e₁))

end Semiformula

structure Hom where
  toFun : M₁ → M₂
  func' : ∀ {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → M₁), toFun (s₁.func f v) = s₂.func f (toFun ∘ v)

notation:25 M " →ₛ[" L "] " M' => Hom L M M'

notation:25 M " ↪ₛ[" L "] " M' => Embedding L M M'

class HomClass (F : Type*) (L : outParam (Language.{u}))
    (M₁ : outParam (Type*)) (M₂ : outParam (Type*)) [s₁ : Structure L M₁] [s₂ : Structure L M₂] [FunLike F M₁ M₂] where
  map_func : ∀ (h : F) {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → M₁), h (func f v) = func f (h ∘ v)

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic.Semantics.Semantics

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

section

variable {L : Language}
variable {M : Type*} {M₁ : Type*} {M₂ : Type*} {M₃ : Type*}
variable [Nonempty M] [Nonempty M₁] [Nonempty M₂] [Nonempty M₃]
  [s : Structure L M] [s₁ : Structure L M₁] [s₂ : Structure L M₂] [s₃ : Structure L M₃]

namespace Structure

variable (L M M₁ M₂ M₃)

structure Hom where
  toFun : M₁ → M₂
  func' : ∀ {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → M₁), toFun (s₁.func f v) = s₂.func f (toFun ∘ v)
  rel' : ∀ {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁), s₁.rel r v → s₂.rel r (toFun ∘ v)

notation:25 M " →ₛ[" L "] " M' => Hom L M M'

structure Embedding extends M₁ →ₛ[L] M₂ where
  toFun_inj : Function.Injective toFun
  rel_inv' {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁) : s₂.rel r (toFun ∘ v) → s₁.rel r v

notation:25 M " ↪ₛ[" L "] " M' => Embedding L M M'

structure Iso extends M₁ ↪ₛ[L] M₂ where
  toFun_bij : Function.Bijective toFun

notation:25 M " ≃ₛ[" L "] " M' => Iso L M M'

@[ext] structure ClosedSubset where
  domain : Set M
  domain_closed : ∀ {k} (f : L.Func k) {v : Fin k → M}, (∀ i, v i ∈ domain) → s.func f v ∈ domain

class HomClass (F : Type*) (L : outParam (Language.{u}))
    (M₁ : outParam (Type*)) (M₂ : outParam (Type*)) [s₁ : Structure L M₁] [s₂ : Structure L M₂] [FunLike F M₁ M₂] where
  map_func : ∀ (h : F) {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → M₁), h (func f v) = func f (h ∘ v)
  map_rel : ∀ (h : F) {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁), s₁.rel r v → s₂.rel r (h ∘ v)

class EmbeddingClass (F : Type*) (L : outParam (Language.{u}))
    (M₁ : outParam (Type*)) (M₂ : outParam (Type*)) [s₁ : Structure L M₁] [s₂ : Structure L M₂] [FunLike F M₁ M₂]
    extends HomClass F L M₁ M₂ where
  map_inj (f : F) : Function.Injective f
  map_rel_inv (f : F) {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁) : s₂.rel r (f ∘ v) → s₁.rel r v

class IsoClass (F : Type*) (L : outParam (Language.{u}))
    (M₁ : outParam (Type*)) (M₂ : outParam (Type*)) [s₁ : Structure L M₁] [s₂ : Structure L M₂] [FunLike F M₁ M₂]
    extends EmbeddingClass F L M₁ M₂ where
  map_bij (f : F) : Function.Bijective f

variable {L M M₁ M₂ M₃}

instance : FunLike (M₁ →ₛ[L] M₂) M₁ M₂ where
  coe := fun φ => φ.toFun
  coe_injective' := fun φ ψ h => by rcases φ; rcases ψ; simp at h ⊢; ext; exact congr_fun h _

instance : HomClass (M₁ →ₛ[L] M₂) L M₁ M₂ where
  map_func := Hom.func'
  map_rel := Hom.rel'

omit [Nonempty M₁] [Nonempty M₂]
@[ext] lemma Hom.ext (φ ψ : M₁ →ₛ[L] M₂) (h : ∀ x, φ x = ψ x) : φ = ψ := DFunLike.ext φ ψ h

namespace HomClass

variable {F : Type*} [FunLike F M₁ M₂] [HomClass F L M₁ M₂] (φ : F)

@[ext] lemma ext (φ ψ : F) (h : ∀ x, φ x = ψ x) : φ = ψ := DFunLike.ext φ ψ h

protected lemma func {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → M₁) :
    φ (s₁.func f v) = s₂.func f (φ ∘ v) := map_func φ f v

protected lemma rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁) :
    s₁.rel r v → s₂.rel r (φ ∘ v) := map_rel φ r v

lemma val_term (e : Fin n → M₁) (ε : ξ → M₁) (t : Semiterm L ξ n) :
    φ (t.val s₁ e ε) = t.val s₂ (φ ∘ e) (φ ∘ ε) := by
  induction t <;> simp [*, Semiterm.val_func, HomClass.func, Function.comp_def]

end HomClass

instance : FunLike (M₁ ↪ₛ[L] M₂) M₁ M₂ where
  coe := fun φ => φ.toFun
  coe_injective' := fun φ ψ h => by rcases φ; rcases ψ; simp at h ⊢; ext; exact congr_fun h _

instance : EmbeddingClass (M₁ ↪ₛ[L] M₂) L M₁ M₂ where
  map_func := fun φ => φ.func'
  map_rel := fun φ => φ.rel'
  map_inj := Embedding.toFun_inj
  map_rel_inv := fun φ => φ.rel_inv'

@[ext] lemma Embedding.ext (φ ψ : M₁ ↪ₛ[L] M₂) (h : ∀ x, φ x = ψ x) : φ = ψ := DFunLike.ext φ ψ h

namespace EmbeddingClass
open HomClass
variable {F : Type*} [FunLike F M₁ M₂] [EmbeddingClass F L M₁ M₂] (φ : F)

def toEmbedding : M₁ ↪ M₂ where
  toFun := φ
  inj'  := map_inj φ

protected lemma func {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → M₁) :
    φ (s₁.func f v) = s₂.func f (φ ∘ v) := map_func φ f v

protected lemma rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁) :
    s₂.rel r (φ ∘ v) ↔ s₁.rel r v := ⟨map_rel_inv φ r v, HomClass.rel φ r v⟩

end EmbeddingClass

instance : FunLike (M₁ ≃ₛ[L] M₂) M₁ M₂ where
  coe := fun φ => φ.toFun
  coe_injective' := fun φ ψ h => by rcases φ; rcases ψ; simp at h ⊢; ext; exact congr_fun h _

instance : IsoClass (M₁ ≃ₛ[L] M₂) L M₁ M₂ where
  map_func := fun φ => φ.func'
  map_rel := fun φ => φ.rel'
  map_inj := fun φ => φ.toFun_inj
  map_rel_inv := fun φ => φ.rel_inv'
  map_bij := fun φ => φ.toFun_bij

@[ext] lemma Iso.ext (φ ψ : M₁ ≃ₛ[L] M₂) (h : ∀ x, φ x = ψ x) : φ = ψ := DFunLike.ext φ ψ h

namespace IsoClass

omit [Nonempty M]

  func := fun k f v => ⟨s.func f (fun i ↦ ↑(v i)), u.closed f (by simp)⟩

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

namespace Structure

variable (L M M₁ M₂ M₃)

structure Hom where
  toFun : M₁ → M₂
  func' : ∀ {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → M₁), toFun (s₁.func f v) = s₂.func f (toFun ∘ v)
  rel' : ∀ {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁), s₁.rel r v → s₂.rel r (toFun ∘ v)

notation:25 M " →ₛ[" L "] " M' => Hom L M M'

structure Embedding extends M₁ →ₛ[L] M₂ where
  toFun_inj : Function.Injective toFun
  rel_inv' {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁) : s₂.rel r (toFun ∘ v) → s₁.rel r v

notation:25 M " ↪ₛ[" L "] " M' => Embedding L M M'

structure Iso extends M₁ ↪ₛ[L] M₂ where
  toFun_bij : Function.Bijective toFun

notation:25 M " ≃ₛ[" L "] " M' => Iso L M M'

@[ext] structure ClosedSubset where
  domain : Set M
  domain_closed : ∀ {k} (f : L.Func k) {v : Fin k → M}, (∀ i, v i ∈ domain) → s.func f v ∈ domain

class HomClass (F : Type*) (L : outParam (Language.{u}))
    (M₁ : outParam (Type*)) (M₂ : outParam (Type*)) [s₁ : Structure L M₁] [s₂ : Structure L M₂] [FunLike F M₁ M₂] where
  map_func : ∀ (h : F) {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → M₁), h (func f v) = func f (h ∘ v)
  map_rel : ∀ (h : F) {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁), s₁.rel r v → s₂.rel r (h ∘ v)

class EmbeddingClass (F : Type*) (L : outParam (Language.{u}))
    (M₁ : outParam (Type*)) (M₂ : outParam (Type*)) [s₁ : Structure L M₁] [s₂ : Structure L M₂] [FunLike F M₁ M₂]
    extends HomClass F L M₁ M₂ where
  map_inj (f : F) : Function.Injective f
  map_rel_inv (f : F) {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁) : s₂.rel r (f ∘ v) → s₁.rel r v

class IsoClass (F : Type*) (L : outParam (Language.{u}))
    (M₁ : outParam (Type*)) (M₂ : outParam (Type*)) [s₁ : Structure L M₁] [s₂ : Structure L M₂] [FunLike F M₁ M₂]
    extends EmbeddingClass F L M₁ M₂ where
  map_bij (f : F) : Function.Bijective f

instance : FunLike (M₁ →ₛ[L] M₂) M₁ M₂ where
  coe := fun φ => φ.toFun
  coe_injective' := fun φ ψ h => by rcases φ; rcases ψ; simp at h ⊢; ext; exact congr_fun h _

  map_rel := Hom.rel'

    φ (s₁.func f v) = s₂.func f (φ ∘ v) := map_func φ f v

protected lemma rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁) :
    s₁.rel r v → s₂.rel r (φ ∘ v) := map_rel φ r v

    φ (t.val s₁ e ε) = t.val s₂ (φ ∘ e) (φ ∘ ε) := by
  induction t <;> simp [*, Semiterm.val_func, HomClass.func, Function.comp_def]

instance : EmbeddingClass (M₁ ↪ₛ[L] M₂) L M₁ M₂ where

structure Hom where
  toFun : M₁ → M₂
  func' : ∀ {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → M₁), toFun (s₁.func f v) = s₂.func f (toFun ∘ v)
  rel' : ∀ {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → M₁), s₁.rel r v → s₂.rel r (toFun ∘ v)

notation:25 M " →ₛ[" L "] " M' => Hom L M M'

have an injective coercion to functions from `α` to `β`.
`FunLike` is the non-dependent version of `DFunLike`.
This typeclass is used in the definition of the homomorphism typeclasses,
such as `ZeroHomClass`, `MulHomClass`, `MonoidHomClass`, ....
-/

C1_dependencies.name: outParam
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

  func' : ∀ {k} (f : L.Func k) (v : Fin k → M₁), toFun (s₁.func f v) = s₂.func f (toFun ∘ v)

/-- The class `FunLike F α β` (`Fun`ction-`Like`) expresses that terms of type `F`
have an injective coercion to functions from `α` to `β`.
`FunLike` is the non-dependent version of `DFunLike`.
This typeclass is used in the definition of the homomorphism typeclasses,
such as `ZeroHomClass`, `MulHomClass`, `MonoidHomClass`, ....
-/
abbrev FunLike F α β := DFunLike F α fun _ => β

C1_dependencies.name: outParam
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

C1_dependencies.name: outParam
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

have an injective coercion to functions from `α` to `β`.

-/

C1_dependencies.name: outParam
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

/-- The class `FunLike F α β` (`Fun`ction-`Like`) expresses that terms of type `F`
have an injective coercion to functions from `α` to `β`.
`FunLike` is the non-dependent version of `DFunLike`.
This typeclass is used in the definition of the homomorphism typeclasses,
such as `ZeroHomClass`, `MulHomClass`, `MonoidHomClass`, ....
-/
abbrev FunLike F α β := DFunLike F α fun _ => β

C1_dependencies.name: outParam
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

C1_dependencies.name: outParam
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

have an injective coercion to functions from `α` to `β`.
`FunLike` is the non-dependent version of `DFunLike`.
This typeclass is used in the definition of the homomorphism typeclasses,
such as `ZeroHomClass`, `MulHomClass`, `MonoidHomClass`, ....
-/
abbrev FunLike F α β := DFunLike F α fun _ => β

C1_dependencies.name: outParam
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

/-- The class `FunLike F α β` (`Fun`ction-`Like`) expresses that terms of type `F`
have an injective coercion to functions from `α` to `β`.
`FunLike` is the non-dependent version of `DFunLike`.
This typeclass is used in the definition of the homomorphism typeclasses,
such as `ZeroHomClass`, `MulHomClass`, `MonoidHomClass`, ....
-/
abbrev FunLike F α β := DFunLike F α fun _ => β

C1_dependencies.name: outParam
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

/-- The class `FunLike F α β` (`Fun`ction-`Like`) expresses that terms of type `F`
have an injective coercion to functions from `α` to `β`.
`FunLike` is the non-dependent version of `DFunLike`.
This typeclass is used in the definition of the homomorphism typeclasses,
such as `ZeroHomClass`, `MulHomClass`, `MonoidHomClass`, ....
-/
abbrev FunLike F α β := DFunLike F α fun _ => β

C1_dependencies.name: outParam
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

C1_dependencies.name: outParam
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

/-- The class `FunLike F α β` (`Fun`ction-`Like`) expresses that terms of type `F`
have an injective coercion to functions from `α` to `β`.
`FunLike` is the non-dependent version of `DFunLike`.
This typeclass is used in the definition of the homomorphism typeclasses,
such as `ZeroHomClass`, `MulHomClass`, `MonoidHomClass`, ....
-/
abbrev FunLike F α β := DFunLike F α fun _ => β

C1_dependencies.name: outParam
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

FunLike
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- The class `FunLike F α β` (`Fun`ction-`Like`) expresses that terms of type `F`
have an injective coercion to functions from `α` to `β`.

/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

-/

C1_dependencies.name: outParam
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

/-- The class `FunLike F α β` (`Fun`ction-`Like`) expresses that terms of type `F`
have an injective coercion to functions from `α` to `β`.
`FunLike` is the non-dependent version of `DFunLike`.
This typeclass is used in the definition of the homomorphism typeclasses,
such as `ZeroHomClass`, `MulHomClass`, `MonoidHomClass`, ....
-/

C1_dependencies.name: outParam
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

-/

C1_dependencies.name: outParam
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

C1_dependencies.name: FunLike
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- The class `FunLike F α β` (`Fun`ction-`Like`) expresses that terms of type `F`
have an injective coercion to functions from `α` to `β`.
`FunLike` is the non-dependent version of `DFunLike`.
This typeclass is used in the definition of the homomorphism typeclasses,

/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

C1_dependencies.name: outParam
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

C1_dependencies.name: outParam
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Gadget for marking output parameters in type classes.

For example, the `Membership` class is defined as:
```
class Membership (α : outParam (Type u)) (γ : Type v)
```
This means that whenever a typeclass goal of the form `Membership ?α ?γ` comes
up, Lean will wait to solve it until `?γ` is known, but then it will run
typeclass inference, and take the first solution it finds, for any value of `?α`,
which thereby determines what `?α` should be.

This expresses that in a term like `a ∈ s`, `s` might be a `Set α` or
`List α` or some other type with a membership operation, and in each case
the "member" type `α` is determined by looking at the container type.
-/
@[reducible] def outParam (α : Sort u) : Sort u := α

informal_statement: If two structures \( M \) and \( N \) are isomorphic (via \( \Theta \)), then they are elementarily equivalent, meaning they satisfy the same first-order sentences in the language \( L \).
informal_proof: Given that \( M \) and \( N \) are isomorphic, there exists a bijective function \( \Theta \) that maps elements and structures of \( M \) to those of \( N \) while preserving all relations and functions defined in \( L \). Elementary equivalence means that for any sentence \( \phi \) in \( L \), if \( M \) satisfies \( \phi \), then \( N \) also satisfies \( \phi \), and conversely. Since \( \Theta \) preserves all these properties, any first-order sentence true in \( M \) will also hold in \( N \), and vice versa. Therefore, \( M \) and \( N \) are elementarily equivalent.

informal_statement: If two models are elementarily equivalent, then they satisfy the same theories.
informal_proof: Given that the models $M_₁$ and $M₂$ are elementarily equivalent, they share identical first-order properties. This means that for any first-order sentence in the language $L$, both models either simultaneously satisfy or do not satisfy the sentence. Consequently, any theory $T$ that is validated by one model is inherently validated by the other, as there is no distinguishing first-order property that could make one model satisfy $T$ while the other does not.

In other words, if two structures satisfy the same first-order sentences over a common language, they agree on the truth value of every formula in that language.

By the definition of elementary equivalence, these models share the same first-order properties. Therefore, for any \( L \)-formula \( \phi \), the satisfaction of \( \phi \) in \( M_1 \) is inherently tied to its satisfaction in \( M_2 \). This ties together the structural similarities of models under elementary equivalence, ensuring that they consistently agree on the truth values of all formulas within the language \( L \).

*Step 1:* Assume that matrix \( M_1 \) is equivalent to \( M_2 \) over \( L \). By definition of equivalence, this means there exists an invertible matrix \( S \) such that:

\[
M_2 = S^{-1} M_1 S
\]

*Step 2:* Similarly, assume that matrix \( M_2 \) is equivalent to \( M_3 \) over \( L \). By definition, there exists an invertible matrix \( T \) such that:

\[
M_3 = T^{-1} M_2 T
\]

*Step 3:* Substitute the expression for \( M_2 \) from Step 1 into the equation in Step 2:

\[
M_3 = T^{-1} (S^{-1} M_1 S) T
\]

*Step 4:* Simplify the equation using the associative property of matrix multiplication:

\[
M_3 = (T^{-1} S^{-1}) M_1 (S T)
\]

*Step 5:* Let \( U = T^{-1} S^{-1} \) and \( V = S T \). Since both \( S \) and \( T \) are invertible, their products and inverses \( U \) and \( V \) are also invertible.

*Step 6:* Therefore, the equation becomes:

\[
M_3 = U^{-1} M_1 V
\]

*Step 7:* This shows that \( M_1 \) is equivalent to \( M_3 \) over \( L \), with the invertible matrices \( U \) and \( V \) establishing the relationship.

*Conclusion:* The equivalence of matrices is transitive, completing the proof.

informal_statement: For any two propositions \( a \) and \( b \), the logical conjunction \( a \land b \) is equivalent to \( b \land a \).
informal_proof:
To establish the commutativity of the logical conjunction, that is, that \( a \land b \) is equivalent to \( b \land a \), we proceed as follows:

1. **Introduce the propositions**: Let \( a \) and \( b \) be any two propositions.
2. **Consider equivalence**: We need to show that \( a \land b \) implies \( b \land a \) and vice versa.
3. **Assume \( a \land b \)**: Suppose both \( a \) and \( b \) are true.
4. **Rearrange the conjunction**: Since both \( a \) and \( b \) are true, it follows that both \( b \) and \( a \) are true, hence \( b \land a \) is true.
5. **Symmetry of implication**: The argument is symmetric for the reverse implication. If \( b \land a \) is true, then both \( b \) and \( a \) are true, so \( a \land b \) is true.

Thus, the conjunction \( a \land b \) is equivalent to \( b \land a \), establishing the commutative property of logical conjunction.

variable (L : Language) (M : Type*) (M₁ : Type*) (M₂ : Type*) (M₃ : Type*) [Nonempty M] [Nonempty M₁] [Nonempty M₂]
  [Nonempty M₃] [s : Structure L M] [s₁ : Structure L M₁] [s₂ : Structure L M₂] [s₃ : Structure L M₃]
informal_statement: For any logical formula φ, being open in the environment defined by s₁ (which involves applying Θ to e₁ and ε₁) is equivalent to being open in the environment defined by s₂. This equivalence holds true across all logical operations such as conjunction (φ ⋏ ψ) and disjunction (φ ⋎ ψ) due to the structural properties preserved by Θ.
informal_proof:
To establish the equivalence, we proceed by induction on the structure of φ, considering various logical operations:

1. **Base Cases**:
   - **True**: The formula represents a tautology, trivially open in any environment because it holds under all possible interpretations.
   - **False**: The formula represents a contradiction, which is never open as it cannot hold under any interpretation.

2. **Logical Connectives**:
   - **Conjunction (φ ⋏ ψ)**:
     - Assume φ ⋏ ψ is open in s₁. This means both φ and ψ are open in s₁, which by the properties of Θ, implies that both φ and ψ are open in s₂ as well. Hence, φ ⋏ ψ is open in s₂.
     - Conversely, if φ ⋏ ψ is open in s₂, both φ and ψ must be open in s₂. Since Θ ensures structural preservation, φ and ψ are open in s₁, making φ ⋏ ψ open in s₁.
   - **Disjunction (φ ⋎ ψ)**:
     - Similar reasoning applies. φ ⋎ ψ being open in s₁ means at least one of φ or ψ is open in s₁. By Θ's structural preservation, at least one remains open in s₂, so φ ⋎ ψ is open in s₂.
     - Conversely, φ ⋎ ψ being open in s₂ ensures at least one of φ or ψ is open in s₂, which, by Θ's properties, implies at least one is open in s₁, making φ ⋎ ψ open in s₁.

3. **Recursive Preservation**:
   - Θ's definition inherently preserves these logical operations. For instance, the composition Θ ∘ e₁ ensures that the evaluation context is suitably transformed without altering the fundamental behavior of φ concerning openness.

By systematically applying these principles to all possible forms of φ, we ensure that the equivalence between φ being open in s₁ and s₂ holds true across the entire logical space covered by the connectives and their combinations.

Thus, the evaluation of φ in the transformed environment s₂ preserves the openness property inherent in s₁ due to the structural integrity maintained by Θ. This completes the proof of the equivalence.

informal_statement: For any term \( t \), the function \( \phi \) applied to the value of \( t \) under some functions \( e \) and \( \varepsilon \) is equal to the value of \( t \) under the transformed functions \( \phi \circ e \) and \( \phi \circ \varepsilon \).
informal_proof:
We prove this statement by induction on the structure of the term \( t \).

1. **Base Case**: If \( t \) is a basic term, the result follows directly from the definitions of \( \texttt{val} \) and the properties of \( \phi \), \( e \), and \( \varepsilon \).

2. **Inductive Step**: Assume the statement holds for all terms smaller than \( t \). We consider the different possible forms of \( t \) according to its definition:
   
   - **Function Application**: If \( t \) is of the form \( f(a) \), then the value of \( \phi(f)(\phi(a)) \) equals \( \phi(\texttt{val}(f \circ a)) \) by the inductive hypothesis and the definitions of \( \texttt{val} \) and composition.
   
   - **Other Cases**: For other forms of \( t \), similar reasoning applies using the definitions of \( \texttt{val} \) and the properties of \( \phi \), \( e \), and \( \varepsilon \).

In each case, the equality \( \phi(\texttt{val}(t)) = \texttt{val}(\phi \circ e \circ t) \) holds, completing the inductive step.

Therefore, by induction, the statement is true for all terms \( t \).

informal_statement: Two functions are equal if and only if they produce the same outputs for the same inputs.
informal_proof:
Let us consider two functions \( f \) and \( g \). Function extensionality states that \( f = g \) if and only if for every input \( x \), \( f(x) = g(x) \). 

1. **Forward Direction**: Assume \( f = g \). Then, by the definition of function equality, for every \( x \), \( f(x) = g(x) \).

2. **Reverse Direction**: Assume for every \( x \), \( f(x) = g(x) \). Then, by the principle of function extensionality, \( f = g \).

Thus, two functions are equal if and only if they produce the same outputs for the same inputs.

informal_statement: The class of closed subsets has been defined as those subsets of a set \( M \) which are preserved under the application of any function \( f \) from a space \( L \) of functions to \( M \). Specifically, a subset \( S \subseteq M \) is closed if, whenever a function \( f \) is applied to any finite collection of elements in \( S \), the result of this function application remains within \( S \).
informal_proof:
This definition is consistent with the standard concept of closure in mathematics, where a set is said to be closed under a particular operation if the operation, when applied to elements of the set, always yields another element within the set. In this case, the "operation" is the application of any function \( f \) from \( L \) to \( M \). By requiring that the image of any such function \( f \) applied to elements of \( S \) remains within \( S \), we ensure that \( S \) maintains this closure property across all possible function applications from \( L \).

This concept is foundational in various areas of mathematics and computer science, particularly in areas where we wish to study the behavior of functions and their interactions with specific subsets of a space. The closure property guarantees that these subsets behave consistently and predictably under the operations defined by the functions in \( L \), making them particularly useful for analysis and construction of more complex structures.

informal_statement: An inductive type can be used to represent the natural numbers, constructing each number starting from zero and building up using a successor function.
informal_proof:
In many type theories, including the one expressed in Lean4, an inductive type provides a means to define complex structures by specifying how they can be constructed from simpler components. For the natural numbers, typically represented as `Nat`, the definition starts with a base element, often denoted as zero, and a successor function that generates the next number in the sequence from any given number.

The successor function ensures that each natural number is unique and distinct, allowing the construction of an infinite set of natural numbers. This is achieved by starting at zero and repeatedly applying the successor function, which adds one to the current number. For example, one is the successor of zero, two is the successor of one, and so on. This process continues indefinitely, accommodating the infinite nature of natural numbers.

The injective nature of the successor function prevents any form of ambiguity; since each number has a unique successor, there are no overlaps or identical elements in the constructed set. This property, combined with the inductive definition, forms the foundational structure for the set of natural numbers within the type theory framework.

Such definitions are not only intuitive but also rigorously justified by the underlying logical principles of the type system, ensuring consistency and reasoned acceptance of the definitions.
